_doc: Hand-curated display layer for The Crucible. Keyed by lab_id. The renderer prefers these polished fields over raw ledger text so the public page is 100% quality. Source of truth stays server/.replications.json; this only controls presentation. 'featured' marks the case-study hero. '_passes' curates the NOT_COMPUTABLE list: only curated passes are shown publicly (the full raw ledger stays in crucible.json).

_passes.match: Generative AI integration into software engineering
_passes.claim: Generative AI is rapidly automating software-engineering tasks
_passes.reason: trend claim, no mechanism to simulate

_passes.claim: Safe-Sora: invisible watermarking for generative video (Su et al. 2025)
_passes.reason: engineering system, not a quantitative mechanism

_passes.claim: Glass-transition duration falls exponentially with cooling rate in a metallic alloy
_passes.reason: claim under-specified for a faithful minimal model

_passes.claim: The AI–biology analogy breaks: brains use local Hebbian synaptic homeostasis
_passes.reason: conceptual claim, no single simulable quantity

ebce40.title: The hot hand is not a fallacy
ebce40.result: Their estimator reads −7.9pp (t=−28) on a shooter with NO hot hand. A measured “zero” is really evidence for a +8.5pp hot hand.
ebce40.canon: For 30 years the canonical finding was that streak shooting is a cognitive illusion: players who feel “hot” are misreading randomness.
ebce40.rebuilt: We rebuilt their exact estimator — P(hit | 3 prior hits) − P(hit | 3 prior misses), averaged per shooting record — and ran it on i.i.d. shooters with provably no hot hand.
ebce40.verdict: On a no-hot-hand shooter the estimator does not read 0; it reads −7.9pp (t=−28 at n=100, growing to −17pp at streak length 4). This is the streak-selection bias of Miller & Sanjurjo (2018): selecting shots that follow a streak inside a finite sequence is a biased sample. A GVT measurement of ~0 therefore implies a real hot hand of roughly +8.5pp. The famous fallacy was the analysis, not the players.

e39390.title: The Dunning–Kruger plot draws itself from pure noise
e39390.result: A null with NO metacognitive deficit reproduces the famous quartile plot and its asymmetry — bottom +45.8 (DK: +46), top −14.2 (DK: −13) — from regression to the mean plus a uniform better-than-average bias. The gaps are predictions, not fits.

7656de.title: Thirty stocks diversify you — until the tails get heavy
7656de.result: N=30 captures ~96% of achievable risk reduction at realistic tails — but only 85% of tail-risk reduction near infinite-variance tails, where ~100 stocks are needed.

4779c1.title: A monkey at a typewriter really does produce Zipf's law
4779c1.result: Random typing yields exponent −1.24; even a natural fine-structure discriminator fails at matched corpus size (1.8× < 2× bar). The deflationary inference survives a severe test.

a3ae64.title: Diversity beats ability — but only at Hong & Page's exact parameters
a3ae64.result: Reproduced in the authors' own relay model: a random team beats the best-individuals team by +1.65 (t=4.1) at the paper's parameters — but the edge is fragile, reversing to −0.38 on a smoother landscape. See the companion FAILED card: the advantage does not survive a different, powered problem model.

e0a43a.title: SGD finds a real minimum of a non-convex loss
e0a43a.result: On a double-well non-convex objective, SGD localizes to a true minimum at the predicted convergence rate.

73f90e.title: Criticality leaves a power-law fingerprint
73f90e.result: At the critical point, fluctuations show power-law scaling and long-range correlations — the signature reproduces cleanly.

7bbc76.title: Sample-efficient policies need far fewer parameters
7bbc76.result: In the low-data regime, online policies match performance with 2–10× fewer total coefficients.

ef9fe3.title: In scale-free networks, the epidemic threshold vanishes
ef9fe3.result: As N grows, λ_c = ⟨k⟩/⟨k²⟩ → 0: a hub-rich network has effectively no herd-immunity threshold.

3f716e.title: LinUCB stays well inside its regret bound
3f716e.result: Measured regret tracks O(√Td·polylog) and sits far below linear-regret baselines.

437d20.title: SGD's slow convergence is a variance floor
437d20.result: Constant-step SGD stalls at a noise floor; variance-reduced methods keep converging — the slowdown is variance, not curvature.

d6e8d6.title: Branching survival collapses onto one curve
d6e8d6.result: Survival probability across sizes collapses onto a single curve in the scaling variable (m−1)·n.

e52111.title: Pulling the hubs shatters the network
e52111.result: Removing the top 10% of nodes by degree multiplies the bond-percolation threshold several-fold (BA, N=2000).

8256e7.title: IT pays off only with organizational change
8256e7.result: Organizational investment, not IT spend alone, drives the return — omitting it inflates the estimated payoff up to 2×.

43c007.title: A simple model beats the fancy one on KB completion
43c007.result: An observed-features model matches or beats latent-feature models on knowledge-base completion.

37ad2a.title: Heavy-tailed waiting times bend the phase transition
37ad2a.result: Non-Markovian spreading with t^(−1−μ) waiting times produces a genuine non-equilibrium phase transition.

b56ae0.title: …but "diversity trumps ability" is not a general law
b56ae0.result: Stress-test of the same claim in a DIFFERENT, faithful problem model (NK landscapes; paired and statistically powered): the best-ability group matches or slightly beats the random/diverse group at every difficulty level. So the Hong-Page advantage is real at the original parameters (companion card) but does NOT generalize — condition-specific, not a universal law, consistent with Thompson (2014). The effect is small; this refutes the universal claim, not the value of diversity in specific regimes.

b790af.title: Metcalfe's Law (network value ∝ n²) is an equal-value artifact
b790af.result: The n² scaling holds only if every pairwise connection has equal value. Under realistic rank-declining connection value the network's value scales as ~n·log n (fitted exponent 1.12, vs 2.00 for equal value; 1.33 for slow decay) — the famous quadratic over-states large-network value, matching Briscoe-Odlyzko-Tilly (2006) and Metcalfe's own 2013 data-fit. A mechanism derivation, not a fit to proprietary network data.

39737a.title: Food nudges are 2.5x more responsive than other domains
39737a.result: From an IDENTICAL true effect in every domain, differential publication bias alone reproduces a 2.63x food/other ratio (control with equal sample sizes = 1.00). The famous 2.5x is a small-study mirage.
39737a.canon: Mertens et al.s widely-cited PNAS meta-analysis reported food-choice nudges are up to 2.5x more responsive to choice architecture than nudges in other domains read as an intrinsic difference in how nudgeable each domain is.
39737a.rebuilt: Smallest model: K domains with an IDENTICAL true effect (Cohen d = 0.20); food studies small-n (per-group ~30, typical point-of-choice field/lab designs), other domains large-n (~300); a study is published iff p < .05 in the expected direction. Then measure the observed food/other inverse-variance-pooled effect ratio.
39737a.verdict: From a true ratio of 1.00, publication bias plus the food-vs-other study-size gap produces an observed ratio of 2.63x. An equal-n control returns 1.00 (the inflation is the sample-size asymmetry, not a sim artifact), and the ratio rises monotonically with that gap (food_n 300->1.01, 100->1.52, 60->1.91, 30->2.64, 20->3.18) the claimed ~2.5x appears precisely at the realistic ~10x asymmetry between small food studies and large other-domain studies. The between-domain RATIO is therefore not robust evidence of intrinsic domain responsiveness. This is a mechanism replication (we lack their raw per-study data) and corroborates the real-data critique of this exact meta-analysis by Maier, Bartos, Stanley, Shanks, Harris & Wagenmakers (2022, PNAS). It does not claim nudges have zero effect only that the domain ranking is fragile to a known confound.

502d6c.title: Good to Great: 11 companies, discoverable shared traits = sustained greatness
502d6c.result: A zero-skill null reproduces the whole pattern: select firms for a 15-year 3.8x-the-market leap from a population where NO firm is more skilled than any other, and their next 15 years revert to the market (forward excess +0.015, 95% CI spanning 0; ~47% beat the market = a coin flip).
502d6c.canon: Collins studied 11 firms that leapt from good to great and stayed there, and distilled shared traits (Level 5 leadership, the Hedgehog Concept, getting the right people on the bus, the Flywheel) presented as the discoverable causes of sustained greatness. ~4M copies sold.
502d6c.rebuilt: Smallest null with skill switched OFF: 1400 firms as geometric random walks with IDENTICAL drift and volatility. Apply Collins-style selection on the dependent variable (mediocre for 15 years, then >= N x the market for the next 15), then measure the NEXT 15 years.
502d6c.verdict: FAILED. The selection cohort is fully reproducible from luck alone (3x->30 firms, 5x->9, vs Collins 11), each spectacular in the selection window (3.8-5.6x the market) BY CONSTRUCTION, after which forward excess collapses to ~0 (3x: +0.015, CI (-1.12,1.64); 5x: -0.008) and only ~47% beat the market going forward. All-firms forward excess = 0.00000 (sanity). This regression-to-the-mean collapse is exactly what happened to Collins' real picks after 2001 (Circuit City bankrupt, Fannie Mae bailed out). Honest scope: the evidence cannot separate skill from luck+selection - NOT that management skill is literally zero. Prior art: Rosenzweig 'The Halo Effect' (2007), Levitt; our contribution is the runnable zero-skill null + forward-collapse receipt.

bf7bb9.title: LLM-as-judge agrees with humans ~80%, so it is a valid quality judge
bf7bb9.result: A zero-understanding null judge that simply picks the LONGER answer already agrees with human preferences 68.1% of the time (vs 50% chance), reproducing ~half of the GPT-4 judges celebrated above-chance agreement; the GPT-4 judge itself agrees with pick-the-longer 73.5% of the time.
bf7bb9.canon: The foundational LLM-as-judge paper reported GPT-4 agrees with human preference judgments ~80% of the time, on par with human-human agreement, and concluded a strong LLM is a valid scalable stand-in for human quality evaluation. LLM-as-judge is now ubiquitous in AI eval.
bf7bb9.rebuilt: On the ORIGINAL released data (lmsys/mt_bench_human_judgments: 3355 human + 2400 GPT-4 pairwise votes), build a NULL judge with zero understanding -> pick the response with more characters. Measure its agreement with human votes and with the GPT-4 judge (ties excluded).
bf7bb9.verdict: FAILED. Length-only vs human = 0.681 (n=2562; robust to word-count, 0.664). GPT-4 judge vs human majority = ~0.84 (n=825) — reproduces the celebrated ~80%, validating the pipeline. Length-only vs GPT-4 = 0.735 (n=1792): the famous judge agrees with the dumb length rule nearly 3/4 of the time. So a rule with NO understanding reproduces ~52-54% of the judges above-chance agreement — the ~80% human-parity is substantially a verbosity/length confound, not proof of semantic judging. Honest scope: length explains about half, not all (residual semantic signal exists); what FAILS is the inference that 80% agreement validates LLM-judges as semantic stand-ins. Prior art: Zheng et al. flag verbosity bias themselves; Dubois et al. 2024 (length-controlled AlpacaEval). Our contribution: the runnable length-only-null receipt on the exact original data.

12b630.title: Founder-led firms returned 3.1x more — the founders mentality drives performance
12b630.result: With IDENTICAL expected returns, a founder-led cohort that is merely ~1.8x as volatile, run through the same survive-and-be-large index filter, shows an apparent 2.60x mean return gap — 76% of Bains 3.1x — from ZERO skill. The advantage is tail-driven: the MEDIAN gap is only 1.58x.
12b630.canon: Bains widely-cited stat: founder-led firms returned about 3.1x more than the rest (1990-2014), presented as evidence that a founders mentality causes superior long-run performance.
12b630.rebuilt: Two cohorts with the SAME expected return; founder-led differs only mechanically — higher volatility (~1.8x) and more delisting. Apply the same look-ahead index rule the stat uses (count only firms that survived to the end and are large enough). Measure the apparent return gap. Pure numpy, no external data.
12b630.verdict: FAILED (with honest scope). A zero-skill survivorship null reproduces a 2.60x MEAN gap (76% of 3.1x), rising monotonically with the volatility ratio (1.4x vol->1.55x; 2.2x->4.77x). Crucially the MEDIAN gap is only 1.58x — the advantage lives in the extreme upper tail, exactly where survivorship operates, and a mean/aggregate 3.1x is the tail-sensitive metric this inflates. So index construction (survivorship + look-ahead inclusion) of a higher-variance cohort manufactures most of the headline with no skill at all. Scope: NOT proof founder firms have zero real edge; assumptions (vol ratio, ruin, index bar) stated and swept. Survivorship bias is textbook; the contribution is the runnable null tied to this specific claim + the mean-vs-median tail diagnosis.
